data.name: Scoregasm
data.detailed_description:
Scoregasm é um incrível e diversificado jogo de tiro com uma galáxia não-linear ramificada em vários caminhos para explorar. É bonito, acessível, divertido e sem dúvida bastante bom! Abre caminho através dos vários níveis da galáxia e usa as tuas habilidades para mudares de rota, descobrires novos níveis, novos inimigos, desbloqueares níveis de desafio extra e combateres os bosses para revelares finais diferentes!

Principais Características:

  • 43 níveis principais variados para descobrir
  • Vários caminhos, explora a galáxia para desbloquear novos níveis!
  • 43 níveis de desafio para desbloquear, um por cada nível principal
  • Mais de 100 inimigos diferentes para encontrar e destruir
  • Proezas que realmente tens que conquistar!
  • Galáxia Secreta para Profissionais
  • 86 Medalhas de Combo, uma em cada nível!
  • 7 possíveis finais - encontra todos os biscoitos e uma nota de £5!
  • Gráficos 3D cheios de estilo
  • Pontuações online para cada modo de jogo e desafio!
  • Compatível com comando/joystick

  • Processor: 2ghz Intel processor (PPC not supported)

reviews.review:
Scoregasm is an energetic twin-stick shooter that puts arcade action, score chasing, and replayability ahead of complicated storytelling. Developed by RC Knight and published by Charlie's Games, it builds its identity around fast battles inside compact arenas where movement, aiming, positioning, and maintaining momentum all matter. The premise is deliberately straightforward: enter a stage, destroy increasingly dangerous enemies, survive the incoming fire, and perform well enough to open additional possibilities across its branching galaxy. That simplicity makes it easy to understand, while the scoring mechanics and escalating difficulty provide considerably more depth for players who want to master it.

Combat is built around constant movement and rapid target selection. Enemies can approach from multiple directions, forcing the player to balance aggressive shooting with careful avoidance. Early encounters are manageable enough to teach the fundamentals, but later stages become much busier as enemy formations and projectiles begin filling the available space. Bullet-hell influences become increasingly noticeable, particularly when surviving requires threading through hazards rather than simply overpowering everything. Controller support is especially appropriate for this style of play, although the Steam version officially lists only partial controller support.

One of the game's best ideas is its nonlinear progression. Rather than sending everyone through exactly the same sequence, performance can affect the path taken through the galaxy. There are 43 main stages to discover, with multiple routes encouraging players to replay the campaign and search for areas they previously missed. Different routes can lead to additional enemies, bosses, bonus content, and multiple conclusions. With seven endings available, reaching the credits once does not represent everything the game has to offer.

The amount of optional material gives the experience much greater longevity than its straightforward presentation might suggest. Every one of the 43 primary stages has an associated challenge level, effectively providing another complete set of scenarios for players interested in testing their skills. More than 100 enemy varieties help prevent the action from becoming completely predictable, while the secret Expert Galaxy provides something more demanding to pursue. There are also 86 Combo Medals, giving completionists a clear incentive to revisit stages and improve their performance rather than simply finishing them.

Scoring is where the design becomes most rewarding. Clearing a stage is satisfying, but learning how to maintain combos and perform more efficiently transforms each encounter into a personal optimization challenge. A run that initially appears excellent may suddenly seem mediocre after discovering a safer route or a better way to preserve a combo. Online scores reinforce this competitive arcade mentality. The result is a game where mechanical improvement becomes its own form of progression, even after much of the regular content has already been discovered.

The visual presentation is uncomplicated but effective. Its colorful 3D environments and energetic effects fit the arcade atmosphere without trying to compete with more technically ambitious shooters. Age is certainly visible in some aspects of the graphics, yet clarity is more important than visual spectacle in a game where identifying enemies and incoming projectiles quickly can determine whether a run continues. The electronic soundtrack also suits the frantic pace and helps give battles a lively rhythm.

There are limitations worth considering. Players looking for substantial storytelling, character development, exploration in the traditional sense, or a cinematic campaign will find very little of that here. The real value comes from repeated play, improving scores, unlocking challenges, finding alternate routes, collecting medals, and eventually tackling harder content. Someone who dislikes replaying stages may therefore exhaust the appeal considerably faster than a dedicated arcade enthusiast.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently Unknown or Unverified for the original game, as its Steam listing does not provide an official Deck compatibility rating. Its modest hardware requirements and controller support may make experimentation through compatibility tools possible, but it should not be treated as officially Steam Deck Verified or Playable. This distinction is particularly important because the newer Son of Scoregasm has received separate Steam Deck-focused improvements, which should not be confused with official support for the original release.

Overall, Scoregasm remains an appealing example of a small arcade shooter achieving longevity through strong mechanical foundations rather than sheer production scale. Its 43 main levels, 43 challenges, branching progression, more than 100 enemy types, secret Expert Galaxy, Combo Medals, bosses, online scoring, and seven endings create an unexpectedly substantial package. It is at its best when treated as something to master rather than simply finish. For fans of twin-stick shooters, bullet-hell action, score attacks, and demanding arcade gameplay, there is a satisfying amount of challenge packed into its modest presentation.

Rating: 8/10
